title: Apollo — all parts (probe)
description: PROBE (R5, #304, 2026-09-26). Generated from knowledge/components/*.meta.json; not canon, not ruled. Per-entry Apollo data sits in x-apollo (an annotation keyword; A2UI ignores it).

Accordion.description: A disclosure control that collapses/expands a section of content behind a titled header. Used to reduce clutter and cognitive load on content-heavy pages or where a range of user needs must be covered (e.g. FAQs). For a single disclosure on its own, prefer an Expand link rather than a lone accordion.

apolloVariant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

AccountCard.description: A passive summary card for a single account: the account label (name · masked number), its balance in the display/amount type, and an optional meta row showing account type (Tags atom) and a RAG status (Status-indicator chip). Surfaced as a missing pattern by the payments-journey gap report.

status.description: Optional RAG status chip in the meta row; meaning carried by the label text, not the dot.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

AccountSelector.description: The from/to account picker of every payment flow plus its compact inline token. Two forms: a SELECTOR (combobox trigger showing the chosen account — name, masked number, balance — opening a listbox of rich account rows; the Dropdown field mechanics with account-shaped options) and a MASKED ACCOUNT CHIP (the chosen account as an inline token for confirmation rows and form summaries). Masked convention promoted from Account-card: middle-dot triple + last four (···4821), never the full number.

label.description: Field label above the trigger ('From account'); part of the combobox accessible name.

form.description: Chip = read-only inline token (role=group + aria-label); selector = the interactive picker.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

accounts.description: The selectable accounts, each supplying name, masked number and balance. | param: Rows of {name, masked, balance}; balances render via the Amount-display primitive (tabular figures, copy-025).

ActionBar.description: A footer bar that pins a screen or flow's primary + secondary actions (e.g. Cancel / Confirm payment). A layout container that composes the Button atom — the bar itself is passive; its buttons carry the interaction. Surfaced as a missing pattern by the journey gap report.

sticky.description: Pin the bar to the bottom of a scrolling flow (position:sticky).

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

actions.description: Holds the screen's primary and secondary actions; the container lays them out but never authors them. | param: 1–3 actions: one primary + optional secondary + optional tertiary (e.g. Back). More than 3 is an anti-pattern.

Alert.description: An in-flow status callout that interrupts nothing: it sits inside the page or form it refers to and stays until resolved or dismissed. The Mono successor to the Legacy Notifications 'contextual' placement — tinted RAG surface, full 1px accent border, status glyph, title + description + optional inline link + optional dismiss. Use Toast for transient confirmations and Banner for page-level persistent messages; use inline field validation (Input-fields) for single-control errors. When: the message is IN FLOW (inside the page or form it refers to) AND it persists until resolved or dismissed AND it carries a status glyph and a title, never colour alone AND an error alert never auto-dismisses

status.description: Binds the R-D20 rag/{status} + rag/{status}-tint pair. Error renders role="alert" (assertive); the rest role="status" (polite).

title.description: Optional bold lead-in (.t-ed-body .em, weight 500). Sentence case.

link.description: Optional inline action link — descriptive text, never 'click here' (aca-004).

dismissible.description: Adds the 24px × in a 44px hit target. Static alerts persist with the task.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

AmountDisplay.description: The money-format PRIMITIVE: renders a currency value consistently — currency symbol/code before the amount with no space (copy-025), tabular lining figures so columns of money align, an unambiguous U+2212 minus for negatives, and a redacted privacy state. Monochrome by design; directional gain/loss colour is owned by the RAG/delta colour workstream and layers on later. Everything from account balances to transaction rows to data-grid numeric cells composes on this atom.

size.description: display = 32px, bound to the .t-cm-figure-4 composite (the display/amount token); default = 16px inline body; small = 14px dense rows/tables.

sign.description: Negative renders a leading U+2212 MINUS in monochrome text — never a colour cue. Positive normally carries no sign; the explicit 'positive' value opts a symbol-carrying monetary value into the ruled green-text seat (s155-D1).

redacted.description: Privacy mask: the value is replaced by dots (aria-hidden) and the element carries role=img + an aria-label giving context (e.g. 'Balance hidden').

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

AmountInput.description: Currency amount entry — the entry twin of Amount-display. Boxed Input-fields chrome with a currency prefix; numerals are tabular figure composites; the value normalises to grouped thousands + two decimals on blur. Banking-critical (itinerary row 17, P1); built Phase-2 wave 1.

size.description: standard = .t-cm-figure-5 (16); display = .t-cm-figure-4 (32) — the payment-journey hero entry.

currency.description: Code before the value, no space (copy-025); symbol (£) closed up. Prefix is aria-hidden — the accessible name carries the currency.

min.description: Validation floor; zero and negatives rejected on entry (a debit renders with the typographic minus −, display only).

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

AnchorNav.description: In-page section navigation with scrollspy: links to headings inside the CURRENT document, where the link matching the section being read marks itself automatically as the reader scrolls. Two placements, one grammar — a sticky horizontal bar and a vertical 'on this page' rail. Use it on long single-page content (product terms, rates and fees, a long article) where the reader needs to see the shape of the page and jump inside it. Itinerary row 37 (P3, 'In-page section nav').

placement.description: Sticky horizontal bar above the content, or a vertical rail beside it. Structural variance — a different assembly, not a scaled parameter.

sections.description: Ordered {id, label} pairs, one per section heading. The ids are real document ids — the links are real fragment links and work with JavaScript off.

currentId.description: The section currently in view. Authored in the markup as the no-JS answer; the scrollspy only ever MOVES it.

offset.description: Pixels of sticky chrome above the content. Drives both scroll-margin-top on the sections and the observer's top rootMargin — one number, two consumers.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

AppShellDoormat.description: The page frame for a marketing or servicing site with more destinations than a masthead can hold. Its proposition is an argument about WHERE NAVIGATION LIVES: four destinations in a sticky masthead, everything else in a mega-footer at the bottom, so the top of the page stays legible and the bottom of the page does real work.

form.description: full = a statement block plus four named groups plus the legal bar. short = three groups and no statement block, for a servicing site whose end matter carries less. ⚠ The mat's own reflow is IDENTICAL in both because it is intrinsic (auto-fit/minmax), not a rule.

primaryNav.description: AT MOST FOUR top-level destinations. The cap is the shell's argument, not a limitation.

doormat.description: Footer in its FULL form. This is the shell's secondary navigation and it must not duplicate the masthead.

AppShellFocused.description: The page frame for one job and nothing else: signing in, entering a passcode, or working through a multi-step task. It is the only shell in the library defined by what it REMOVES — no primary navigation, no breadcrumb, no utility group, no search. One identity, one deliberate way out, and the task. When: primaryNavigation = absent AND breadcrumbs = absent AND search = absent AND exits = 1 AND job.count = 1

form.description: auth = a 420px column with no progress band; the task is short enough that 'how far through am I' is not a question anyone asks. task = a 720px column with the progress band under the masthead. The difference is a BAND, not a layout.

brand.description: the masthead identity — the official masterbrand asset, bound #230 (masterbrand-light-colour on light chrome, masterbrand-dark-colour on dark).

exit.description: the ONE way out. A labelled control whose accessible name says what leaving does.

AppShellMultiColumn.description: The list-and-detail frame: a navigation rail, a master list of records, and a detail pane showing the one record the list is currently pointing at — collapsing to a single pane on a phone, where choosing a row replaces the list with the detail and a back control returns. Itinerary row 99's own notes cell is 'List + detail frame.'

railed.description: whether the nav rail is present as a third column. It is a rail rather than an expanded column by construction — three columns is already the widest thing this frame can be, and a 248px column would take the room the list needs.

endMatter.description: Footer in its slim form, as the LAST CHILD OF `.sh` so it spans all three panes — the rail, the list and the detail are peers and none of them is 'the content column'. The doormat form fits the same slot.

AppShellNavRail.description: The page frame for a dense application that cannot spare 248px to a sidebar. A permanent 64px icon rail carries the navigation, and a flyout carries the names the icons cannot. It is not App-shell-side-nav's collapsed state — there is no expand toggle, and that absence is the component.

AppShellSideNav.description: The desktop application frame: a persistent vertical navigation column beside a content region, under a compact app bar. Itinerary row 98's own notes cell is 'Desktop app frame.' The column is Sidebar-nav, unmodified; what this artefact adds is the RULE by which the column expands, collapses to a rail, or leaves the layout for a drawer.

AppShellSplit.description: The page frame for a task that needs two things on screen at once, with neither subordinate to the other: a payment file beside its validation report, a document beside its history, a monitor above its log. The user, not the layout, decides how the room is divided, and the division is published as a percentage so it survives a resize and an axis change.

AppShellTopNav.description: The page frame for an application whose primary navigation lives across the top: a masthead band carrying the brand, the primary destinations and the utility actions, optionally a second band when the nav outgrows one row, optionally a third band of section nav, then the wayfinding trail, then the content region, then the end matter. It is the thing content lives inside — itinerary row 99's sibling and row 97's own notes cell, 'Frame content lives in.' When: destinations <= 7 AND nav.levels <= 2

Stacking b

Avatar.description: Represents a user or entity in a compact, typically circular form. Three content variants — an uploaded image, the user's initials, or a placeholder icon — in three sizes, with on-light and on-dark treatments.

apolloVariant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

AvatarGroup.description: A set of people shown as one object: overlapping Avatar discs, primary-first, with an overflow counter when the set is longer than the display cap. The unit of meaning is the GROUP ('five people are on this approval'), not the individuals.

size.description: 32 / 44 / 64 — Avatar's own ramp, copied exactly. Overlap follows at -8 / -12 / -16 (a quarter of the disc), so a member always shows enough of itself to read as a separate person.

max.description: Display cap. Members beyond it collapse into the overflow counter. 3 is a specimen choice, not a ruled default.

interactive.description: ⛔ 'members' is offered at MEDIUM and LARGE ONLY — a 32px interactive disc breaches the ruled 44px min-hit-area. Small sets that must be clickable take 'group': one 44px target for the whole stack.

announce.description: ⚠ TWO ACCESSIBLE SHAPES FOR ONE COMPONENT — a decision, not a feature. See $openQuestions.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

BackToTop.description: A page-chrome utility that appears once the reader has scrolled past a threshold and returns them to the top of the scrollable region on activation. PROPOSED #209 (itinerary row 38, slug back-to-top) — NOT GATED, NOT RULED. An Icon-button idiom, per the wave-3 brief: SECONDARY tier tokens (deliberately not primary — this is chrome, never the primary action of a view), 44x44 target and B-D7 press-physics copied verbatim from Icon-button.reference.

glyph.description: Icon id from the assets/icons sprite. Specimen uses arrows-and-chevrons/arrow-up.svg.

scrollTarget.description: aria-controls id of the scrollable region this control acts on — the whole page, or a scoped scrollable panel.

threshold.description: ⛔ UNSPECIFIED store-wide. The scroll distance (px or viewport-heights) past which the control fades in is a UX-writing / Dave call, not resolved here. The demo uses an arbitrary 200px scrollTop for illustration only.

visible.description: Drives the is-hidden/is-visible fade; true once past `threshold`.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

Badge.description: A small visual indicator that passively notifies users of new activity relating to a specific UI element, directing them to find out more (e.g. a badge by the inbox link when a new message arrives). Two forms: a simple dot, or a number for a count. Can also sit on an icon.

size.description: Only on the '.Badge on icon' variant — small 10px, medium 13px, large 20px. The standalone Badge is 12px (simple) / 20px (number).

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

Banner.description: The page-level, persistent member of the feedback family: a full-width solid RAG surface that sits above the content it governs and stays until the condition clears or the user dismisses it. Use for conditions that apply to the whole page or session (service outage, device verification, expiring card) — not for in-flow validation (Alert) or transient confirmations (Toast).

status.description: Binds the R-D20 rag/{status}-background fill + its most specific ruled ink (see tokens). Error renders role="alert".

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

actions.description: Holds the banner's response actions; the container lays them out but never authors them. | param: Up to two ghost actions — mutually exclusive with dismiss (Legacy family shape rule kept).

Breadcrumbs.description: Secondary navigation showing the user's location within the site hierarchy and letting them step back to ancestor pages. A row of breadcrumb levels (links) separated by a divider, ending in the current page (a non-link). When: shape = ancestor-path × links AND depth >= 2

state.description: Per .Breadcrumb level. 'no-link' = the current/last item (non-clickable). Hover and Pressed share a single combined state.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

Button.description: A control that triggers an action. Four emphasis levels form a hierarchy — primary (highest emphasis, the main action), secondary, tertiary (outlined), and quaternary (lowest emphasis / borderless). Available on-light and on-dark, in a default and a Large size. When: emphasis in (primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary) AND label = text

state.description: processing + success seen on primary (rag/success); confirm which states apply to each type.

size.description: default height 44px; 'Large' variant exists for primary (and likely all types) — confirm Large height.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

Calendar.description: The standalone month grid: a whole month, in page flow, sized by its container. Weekday heads, whole week rows (out-of-month days drawn, not hidden), full keyboard grid navigation, month and year paging, ink-knockout selection, a structural today ring and a disabled treatment for out-of-range days. Built #210 wave 4 (heavy seven). PROPOSED, NOT RULED — nothing is registered and every question in the receipt is Dave's.

month.description: The month in view. Week starts Monday (en-GB), as Date-picker does.

value.description: The selected day, or nothing. Single selection only — range selection is NOT drawn and is not this component's claim (see Date-range picker, and receipt Q5).

minDate/maxDate.description: Days outside the range render disabled (text/disabled, the Date-picker treatment, in lock-step). The live specimen disables everything before today so the treatment is visible — a demo choice, not a rule.

showAdjacentMonths.description: PROPOSED default. True draws the leading and trailing days of the neighbouring months at a readable recessive ink so week rows are whole; false would leave holes in the grid the way Date-picker's panel does. Receipt Q3 asks Dave which is the house default and whether those days should be selectable.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

CardHeaderLockup.description: The header zone of a Cards surface — title, an optional meta line, and either inline ghost actions or a single overflow trigger that opens an actions menu — kept separate from Cards' four full card types because a header zone recurs inside many different card bodies. Composed ENTIRELY from Cards, Icon-button, Status-indicator and Dropdown's floating-panel CSS (with a declared ARIA deviation from listbox to menu). Itinerary row 117 (Layer 2, NO-ARTEFACT-CLASS at mint; PROPOSED here, not ruled).

arrangement.description: Three arrangement variants: A title+meta only, B title+meta+two inline ghost actions (Cards' .qbtn), C title+meta+status chip+overflow menu. VARIANTS-axis prop (s142-D1 class C6).

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

Cards.description: A family of container components that group related content (and optionally an action) into a bordered surface. Five types covering interactive and static use, with and without imagery.

state.description: Interactive types only (basic, actions). Non-interactive/image-static types are default-only.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

content.description: The grouped content the card surface frames. | param: Content combinations seen on actions/basic cards.

Carousel.description: A slide container that shows one item of a set at a time (or a peeking neighbour, in the peek/snap variant), navigated by dot buttons, prev/next arrows, or keyboard — with aria-roledescription="carousel" semantics per the APG carousel pattern. PROPOSED at #210 wave-4 lane C; not registered, not ruled.

variant.description: standard = one slide fills the viewport, transform/hidden-driven, JS owns every position change. peek = native CSS scroll-snap-type:x mandatory, neighbour slides visible at both edges; JS only mirrors dot state via IntersectionObserver so direct swipe/scroll and the buttons never disagree.

slideCount.description: Drives the dot row and the aria-label "N of M" on each slide; authoring-time, not user-facing.

autoplay.description: PROPOSED DEFAULT OFF, not built as an option in this snippet. Dave's — see the receipt's $decisionsForDave: does an opt-in autoplay variant belong in the library at all, given WCAG 2.2.2 timing-adjustable and the mixed UX record of autoplaying carousels.

Cascader.description: Choose ONE PATH through a hierarchy, one level per column. The trigger shows the committed path; the panel shows each level beside the last, so the shape of the data is visible while the choice is being made. Use it where the answer is a location in a tree — a holding location, a category and sub-category, an org unit — and where showing the whole tree at once would be more than the question needs.

levels.description: The reference draws three (region / nation / city). Nothing in the CSS or the JS is bound to three; the column row takes as many <ul class="cs-col"> as it is given.

state.description: Same state channel as the gated Dropdown/Multi-select field — inherited, not re-specified. NO ERROR STATE IS DRAWN: the error grammar for this field would be Input-fields', unchanged, and drawing it here would be a fourth copy of it.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

ChartBar.description: Categorical comparison as vertical columns or horizontal bars, single- or multi-series (grouped + stacked), with the full Layer-2 interaction layer restored to match the Chart-line exemplar (chart-revisit wave, 2026-07-24). Semantic SVG in the DOM, styled by tokens, animated by CSS, behaviour by the ONE generated dv-behaviour partial (ADR-0015), described by a real table. PROVISIONAL-AGENT: promoted from the PARKED kit (9 rounds, not signed off); kit geometry OBSERVED, Layer-2 + rulings receipted. When: answers = comparison AND axis.x = categorical

orientation.description: column = vertical single-series; bar = horizontal single-series (positives only, dv-bar-007); grouped-column + stacked-column = multi-series (D-Q3 promote).

sort.description: Menu 3/4 sort: BAKED VARIANT GROUPS (data-dv-view — geometry is generation-time), switched by a seg control that CONSUMES the Segmented-control atom; the table mirrors the active order via baked <tbody data-dv-view> variants.

empty.description: No-data state consumes the Empty-state pattern by reference.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

series.description: One or more series drawn grouped or stacked across the categorical axis. | param: categorical = data/series/1–5 (mode-stable isoluminant, R-D9); status = the salience RAMP red › amber › green › blue on rag/* (R-D9); multi = grouped/stacked use series/1–3 with shaped+lettered legend keys and legend-as-filter.

data.description: Carries the category values per series the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes. | param: A real <table class="dv-table"> inside the figure — the a11y spine AND the tabular alternative (dv-005). Surfaced by the TABLE-VIEW POPOVER (dropdown w/ solid rotating arrow, static label; surface card, Esc-dismiss) — the exemplar's, not a native <details>.

ChartBoxplot.description: Statistical distribution per category — median, interquartile range, whiskers, and outliers — as a real SVG box plot. NET-NEW, chart-expansion programme WAVE 2 lane ② (statistical/gauge), 2026-08-05. Built to the Chart-scatter Layer-1 pattern (toolbar + table spine); PROVISIONAL-AGENT pending Dave's eyeball and conductor registration. When: answers = distribution AND categories >= 2 AND each category carries a five-number summary AND span.cols <= 8

outliers.description: Points falling outside the whiskers, plotted individually. | param: Points outside the whisker range, drawn with the Chart-scatter ENLARGED marker family (circle r5.5, page-colour stroke) — same series, not a new colour channel.

data.description: Carries the five-number summary per category the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes. | param: Real <table class="dv-table"> mirroring the five-number summary + outliers per category (dv-005).

ChartBullet.description: KPI performance at a glance — a measure bar against a comparative target marker and qualitative performance ranges. NET-NEW, chart-expansion programme WAVE 2 lane ② (statistical/gauge), 2026-08-05. Built to the Chart-scatter Layer-1 pattern (toolbar + table spine); PROVISIONAL-AGENT pending Dave's eyeball and conductor registration. When: answers=comparison AND the reading is one measure against a target plus qualitative performance bands AND span.cols 4–6

target.description: Comparative marker — a 3px vertical ink tick spanning the row (brief-ruled: 'marker = ink').

empty.description: No-data state = the Empty-state pattern by reference.

rows.description: One measure/target row per KPI shown in the bullet stack. | param: One row per KPI: measure, target, and three qualitative range breakpoints.

ranges.description: The banded qualitative ranges each measure bar is read against. | param: Qualitative bands (poor/satisfactory/good) BEHIND the measure — CANON greys (#96-D1 ③ RULED), z-order bands→bar→marker confirmed correct (DOM paint order).

Footer.description: The APP FOOTER: the contentinfo landmark at the bottom of an authenticated application's content column, carrying what an operator needs at the one moment they look down — WHAT AM I LOOKING AT, IS IT REAL, AND HOW OLD IS IT? Headers.description: App-only header components that title and frame a screen or section. Hero.description: A large, responsive marketing banner at the top of a page, carrying a primary message (headline + intro + CTA) over an image or video, with an optional secondary message. Fully responsive across breakpoints with fixed- or full-height variants.

breakpoint.description: Responsive hero artboards: XL (scale-3), M & L (scale-2), MS (scale-1), S & XS (scale-1).

HeroVariants.description: Composes/extends the gated Hero baseline into four arrangements (baseline, media, stat-led, CTA-led) without adjudicating whether they become sub-variants of one Hero organism or stay separate. Every headline/intro/CTA/arrow-link markup traces to Hero.reference.html unchanged; the media, stat-led and CTA-led forms add borrowed atoms (Layout-utilities l-split, Stat-card, Button) around it. Itinerary row 118 (Layer 2, NO-ARTEFACT-CLASS at mint; PROPOSED here, not ruled). Do-not-rule: 'Hero component EXISTS — variants compose/extend it, relationship PROPOSED, no adjudication.'

IconButton.description: An icon-only control that triggers a single action where space is tight or the action is universally recognised (add, download, edit, search, close). Shares Button's four-level emphasis hierarchy (primary / secondary / tertiary / quaternary) and its tokens, but carries no visible label — so it must supply an accessible name and guarantee a 44x44 target. Use a labelled Button when the action is not unambiguous from a glyph alone. When: the control performs an action AND space is tight OR the glyph is universal AND an accessible name is supplied AND the hit target is at least 44x44 AND a tooltip carries the label

glyph.description: Icon id from the assets/icons sprite; drives the accessible name unless aria-label overrides.

PROPOSED at #210 wave-4 lane C; not registered, not ruled.

InputFields.description: Text-entry form controls and their label. Family: single-line input (standard + large), multi-line input, date-picker input (with calendar day cells, nav arrows, and a modal/dropdown calendar), and the input label. Full state set: default, hover, active, completed, disabled, error. When: entry = free text AND expected answer fits ONE line AND no fixed option list exists AND the value is not money, a date, a time or a secret

When: shape = one-measure × value-delta-and-series AND series != none

Popover.description: Rich anchored content that opens on CLICK — Tooltip's interactive sibling. Where a Tooltip annotates a label with plain text on hover/focus, a Popover holds structured, focusable content (title, body, link, dismiss) as a non-modal dialog anchored to its trigger. If the user can act inside it, it is a Popover; if it is a sentence of help text, it is a Tooltip; if it must interrupt, it is a Modal. When: the content is STRUCTURED and FOCUSABLE AND it opens on CLICK from a labelled trigger AND it does not scroll AND it is non-modal (no focus trap, no aria-modal) AND only one is open

ProgressBar.description: THE PROGRESS READING OF THE ONE METER MOLECULE. Use this when the value is a task underway and a full bar means DONE — uploads, downloads, multi-part transfers, savings goals, completeness scores. The geometry, the tokens, the states and the full spec live ONCE, in meter.meta.json; this record exists so 'Progress bar' stays a findable, selectable identity in the catalogue with its own category, per s210-D5.

ProgressTracker.description: Shows users how far they are through a multi-step process by filling a segmented track and labelling the current step (e.g. 'Step 2 of 4').

QrCode.description: Show a string as a machine-readable square so a second device can pick it up — a link, a reference, an enrolment code. The component's whole job is to stay SCANNABLE: real modules at a real size, with the quiet zone carried inside the artwork, and the same content repeated as text for anyone who is not going to point a camera at a screen.

value.description: The encoded string. It determines the symbol VERSION and therefore the module count: 23 characters gives a 25x25 version-2 symbol, 39 characters a 29x29 version-3 one. The component cannot be given a fixed module count.

size.description: A MODULE size, not a box size: 4px, 8px and 12px per module. The pixel box is derived (module size x unit count) and never typed. Two payloads of different lengths at the same size are physically different sizes, and that is correct.

errorCorrection.description: UNRULED. M is used throughout. The level trades symbol size against damage tolerance; a centre logo or lockup would REQUIRE level H and is not drawn here.

quietZone.description: In MODULES, and it is inside the viewBox, not padding around it. Four is the ISO/IEC 18004 minimum. It is not exposed as something a consumer should reduce; it is a prop only because the number should be visible rather than buried.

valueLow.description: The low handle's current value. Clamped so it can never exceed valueHigh (authored JS, see behaviour).

valueHigh.description: The high handle's current value. Clamped so it can never fall below valueLow.

unit.description: Prefix/suffix for the displayed value pair, e.g. '£'. Specimen shows GBP; not itself a currency-formatting component.

disabled.description: NOT DRAWN as a specimen this pass — the gated Slider has no disabled specimen either; carried as a declared gap, not invented here to avoid drifting ahead of its own precedent.

RunwayBar.description: A READOUT that answers one question: does the money cover what is already scheduled, and until when? It states a verdict with a date, shows the arithmetic that produces it (balance − committed = buffer), and draws the split on a bar. ⚠ THE BAR IS A GATED Progress-bar, COPIED BYTE-FOR-BYTE — this component draws no new bar. What it adds is the verdict, the arithmetic and the legend. PROPOSED #204 (itinerary row 94, slug runway-bar) — NOT GATED, NOT RULED, AND ITS PROVENANCE IS A TEST FIXTURE (see provenance). Fintech semantics are Dave's (the Kpi-tile precedent, s182-D2). When: answers = one-number AND shape = one-measure × committed-vs-balance-split AND verdict != none

committed.description: The fill — aria-valuenow. ⚠ CLAMPED to balance in the SHORT state, because a progressbar cannot express overflow. The true figure appears in the legend, the arithmetic and aria-valuetext.

buffer.description: Derived: balance − committed. Rendered through the Amount-display money-format primitive (symbol before, no space, tabular lining, U+2212 minus, MONOCHROME).

verdict.description: ★ THE POINT OF THE COMPONENT. A WORD AND A DATE — 'Covered through 31 May', 'Covered to 24 May', 'Short from 12 May'. Never a colour on its own.

verdictTone.description: Renders the Status-indicator RAG-tint chip. ⛔ WHICH VERDICT MAPS TO WHICH TONE IS A SEMANTIC BINDING AND IS DAVE'S — proposed here, not ruled.

showMath.description: The balance/committed/buffer definition list. Turning it off makes this a Progress bar (see antiPatterns).

Use for switching a presentation, scale, or range in place (not for navigation between destinations — that is Tabs).

Distinct from Loading-indicator (use that when there is no known layout to mirror) and from the queued loader atom (spinners — GOOD-MORNING §C·3b): a skeleton never spins.

A Button + Dropdown composition, per the wave-3 brief: the main/caret pair reuses Button.reference's tokens verbatim, and the flyout reuses Dropdown.reference's `.menu` shell verbatim, with role="menu"/"menuitem" replacing role="listbox"/"option" because a split-button menu triggers ACTIONS, not a value selection.

Splitter.description: Let the reader decide how much room each of two panes gets. A draggable, keyboard-resizable divider sits between them, publishes where the boundary is, and refuses to let either pane disappear. Use it where two things must stay on screen together and the right balance between them is the reader's business, not the layout's — a list and the record it opens, a filter panel and its results.

orientation.description: Names the SPLIT, not the bar. `horizontal` = two panes side by side, divided by a VERTICAL bar (which is what aria-orientation then says). `vertical` = two panes stacked, divided by a HORIZONTAL bar. The naming is a known trap and is stated on the snippet's face.

value.description: The primary pane's size as a PERCENTAGE of the container, 0-100. Authored in the markup as aria-valuenow; the component reads it from there at start-up, so the markup is the source of truth and not a JS default.

minPrimary.description: CSS custom property --min-pri. A 4px multiple. The pointer drag and the keyboard use the SAME clamp, so a mouse cannot reach a size a keyboard cannot.

thickness.description: CSS custom property --div: the DRAWN rule. The POINTER target is separately 24px via a hit pseudo-element.

step.description: Arrow-key increment; shift+arrow is 64px. Both 4px multiples.

collapsible.description: Enter on the divider collapses the primary pane to zero and restores it to the size it had. The separator is never removed when a pane collapses, so there is always a way back.

state.description: `disabled` keeps the separator and its accessible name — the boundary still exists — but removes the tab stop, the cursor and the grip, and sets aria-disabled.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

StandingOrderMandateRow.description: A RECURRING PAYMENT INSTRUCTION THAT HAS NOT HAPPENED YET: who is paid, how much, on what rhythm, when next, and what state the instruction is in. Two actions per row — open the mandate, or manage it. PROPOSED #209 (itinerary row 95, slug standing-order-mandate-row, P3) — NOT GATED, NOT RULED. Fintech semantics are Dave's (the Kpi-tile precedent, s182-D2).

payee.description: The row's subject. It must never be the element that gives way when chips crowd the line — see antiPatterns and knownFindings.

mandateType.description: ⛔ NOT COSMETIC. A standing order is the customer's own instruction (fixed amount, fixed rhythm, the customer controls it); a Direct Debit is a mandate granted to a PAYEE who pulls a VARIABLE amount under the Direct Debit Guarantee. Legally and operationally different objects. Rendered as a Tags atom

amount.description: MONOCHROME, always. Amount-display's format via Runway-bar: symbol before the amount with no space (copy-025), tabular lining figures, U+2212 for the minus. No coloured monetary seat is bound anywhere in this component.

amountIsVariable.description: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P2). A variable Direct Debit shows the LAST taken figure and says 'Amount varies' in the rhythm line, rather than presenting a stale number as if it were the next one. Which figure a variable mandate should show is Dave's.

nextDate.description: The row's date is in the FUTURE and is a PROMISE — that is the tell against the gated transaction row, whose date is in the past and is a fact.

status.description: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P4). manageAction.description: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P5). Drawn as a trailing 44×44 icon-button carrying the byte-matched global-controls/menu-more-horizontal.svg glyph with an accessible name. Alternatives Dave may prefer: a text button ('Manage'), no control at all with the actions on the detail page, or a real Dropdown menu.

delta.description: Signed change + direction word ('+12.4% up'); .t-cm-figure-6 in INK. Direction = arrow + sign + wording, never colour alone.

direction.description: R-D5: directional deltas are red/green ONLY. The arrow glyph wears rag/success or rag/error (3:1 floor, R-D6 A′ — labelled); flat = no arrow, 'No change'.

Stepper.description: The interactive multi-step flow driver (Progress-tracker is display-only): step content panels, validation-gated Next, back-navigation on completed dots, and the same dots↔track responsive collapse. Back/Next ride the Mono button ladder as the journey's real actions. Itinerary row 34 (P1); built Phase-2 wave 2 (worker A continuation).

backNavigation.description: Completed dots are real buttons; current and future steps are never clickable.

Summary.description: A key/value list for confirming details before or after an action (a payment review, a receipt). Name on the left (text/secondary), value on the right (text/default, tabular-nums), hairline dividers between rows, with an optional emphasised total row.
