items.description: The 3-5 equal-width destinations, each an icon plus label. | param: 3–5 destinations. Fewer than 3 isn't a tab bar; more than 5 crowds the targets.

Table.description: Data tables let users scan, analyse and compare data. Header / sub-header / data cells arranged with a first-row header, a first-column header, or both; cells can be left- or right-aligned (right for numeric).

Tabs.description: Let users switch between peer views/panels within the same context. A horizontal tab bar with a selected indicator, a bottom track, and an overflow dropdown when tabs exceed the available width.

overflow.description: Overflow dropdown (with menu items) when tabs don't fit.

label.description: Tabs can be label or icon-only.

Tags.description: Surface keyword descriptors that tell the user about an item's content composition and its relationship to a broader content structure. Static Tag (label) or interactive Tag link, with or without a background fill.

type.description: Tag = static label; Tag link = interactive (navigates/filters), has hover/pressed.

background.description: Background=true draws a filled chip; false is text-only.

state.description: Tag link only (hover & pressed combined).

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TagsInput.description: A field the user types free values into, each committed as a removable chip. Use it where the vocabulary is the user's own — payment references, labels, search terms — and no list can be offered. The gated Tags atom is the display half of this: same chip, no field.

commitKeys.description: Comma is included because reference lists are habitually comma-separated; blur also commits a pending value rather than discarding it.

state.description: Same state channel as Input-fields/Textarea — inherited.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TemplateAuth.description: The unauthenticated entry pages: log on, register, and one-time passcode. A quiet brand column beside a single narrow form column, collapsing to one column. It contributes page-scale layout and the brand placement; every control inside it is a gated component, borrowed.

screen.description: All three are drawn in the snippet, each in its own frame, so they can be compared side by side.

brandColumn.description: The quiet column carrying the official mark. Collapses ABOVE the form at container <=880px; source order is already correct so no reordering is needed.

revealPassword.description: A TEXT toggle, not a glyph - the library has no visibility icon (see accessibility.$noVisibilityGlyph). Its label states the NEXT action and aria-pressed states the CURRENT one.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TemplateConfirmation.description: The page at the end of an instruction, in two states. Confirmation is a 380px column that ENDS a flow; a confirmation PAGE has to be the RECEIPT as well, so the ORDER changes and that order is the template's whole contribution: message column, then the FACTS, then the actions, then what happens next. Actions come after the facts because a person cannot decide what to do until they have read what was done. When: position = end of an instruction AND order = message, then FACTS, then actions, then what-happens-next AND a reference is shown if one exists

variant.description: SUCCESS keeps Confirmation's rag/success roundel and its entrance animation. PENDING takes NO success device - see antiPatterns.

nextSteps.description: An ORDERED list, because the steps are ordered and a bulleted list would say they are not.

apolloVariant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TemplateCreateEdit.description: The page a person fills in to CREATE a new record, and the same page re-entered to EDIT an existing one. It is an organism-of-organisms: an app bar, a page-head lock-up, a form column beside a guidance aside, and an action bar that stays reachable. It contributes page-scale LAYOUT and nothing else - every control inside it is a gated component, borrowed.

mode.description: CREATE starts empty and its action bar is Cancel + Save. EDIT arrives prefilled, gains an unsaved-changes strip on first edit, gains a destructive action pushed to the far edge, and may lock fields whose change is a different journey. Both are drawn in the snippet.

guidance.description: Whether the guidance aside is present. When absent the form column takes the full width; when present it is 320px and moves BELOW the form at container <=880px.

destructiveAction.description: EDIT only. Rendered with .fl-spacer so it sits at the opposite edge from Save and is never adjacent to it.

stickyActions.description: The action bar is position:sticky against the nearest SCROLLPORT. On a real page that is the page. See the antiPattern about reference pages.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TemplateDashboard.description: A PAGE-SCALE ORGANISM for an overview screen: a page header lock-up, a board of Kpi-tiles, a chart panel beside a summary rail, and a Data-grid of recent records. Its question is 'how are things, and what needs me?', which is a question about SEVERAL records at once — that is what separates it from the detail template. Composed entirely from existing components; the only new CSS is thirteen composition rules, each a relationship between panels.

kpis.description: PROPOSED, NOT RULED. Four are drawn because the auto-fill grid reflows 4 → 3 → 1 and that is the collapse worth proving. WHICH four figures a business overview leads with is a product decision and is Dave's.

period.description: PROPOSED. Rendered as a View-options `.seg` switcher. The switcher is INERT on this page — the behaviour is View-options'.

chart.description: PROPOSED. Drawn as Chart-bar's COLUMN specimen. ⚠ The H-BAR specimen was composed first and rejected by looking: without Chart-bar's fit engine its left-hand category labels clip to 'oceries' / 'nsport' / 'ousing'. A template that does not host the engine must choose a specimen that does not need it

rail.description: PROPOSED. Balances (a Summary) plus a needs-attention list (Status-indicator chips). What belongs in a rail, and whether there should be one, is Dave's.

grid.description: PROPOSED. A Data-grid drawn in a real resting state — two filters applied, sorted by date descending, page 1 of 4. Sorting and paging are Data-grid's behaviour and are not hosted here.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TemplateDashboardBento.description: A PAGE-SCALE ORGANISM for an overview screen BUILT ON THE BENTO GRAMMAR: a masthead, a page header lock-up, and one dashboard-role bento wall whose tiles are themselves bentos - the bento-of-bentos s217-D2/D3 describe. It answers the same question as Template dashboard ('how are things, and what needs me?') and differs in ONE thing: its layout is canon's .c-bento structural component rather than a Layout-utilities grid. It exists because the #230 rehearsal measured that `grep -rl '\.c-bento' knowledge/snippets/` returned ZERO files, so a cold builder told to copy component markup had nothing to copy for a bento dashboard.

groups.description: PROPOSED. Three sub-bentos are drawn (KPI board, chart, position rail) because three is the smallest number that shows a full-width group AND a side-by-side pair. HOW MANY groups a dashboard has, and what belongs in each, is a product decision and is Dave's.

mainSpacing.description: The s219-D1(4) ruled spacing rail, six stops. 40 is mono's ruled dashboard default. The edit pass picks among stops; a free value is not reachable and widening the set is a ruling.

subSpacing.description: Same rail. 4 is mono's ruled dashboard sub default (s219-D1(5)).

keylines.description: s219-D2(4): OFF on every dashboard in every theme. The switch is available in edit mode per s219-D1(2), but the ON construction is not drawn here - see $bentoGrammar.keylines.

chart.description: PROPOSED. Chart-bar's COLUMN specimen, spliced. The chart is NOT made fluid: without Chart-bar's fit engine a width:100% SVG scales its own text and strokes, which is the banned physics _RUNBOOK-render-verify.md records. It scrolls inside its module.

rail.description: PROPOSED. A Summary of balances plus a needs-attention list of Status-indicator chips, stacked inside their own sub-bento.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TemplateDetail.description: A PAGE-SCALE ORGANISM for ONE record: a page header lock-up carrying the record's identity and its status, a Tabs strip, a Summary of the facts, a Timeline of what has happened to it, and a rail of Document-rows for what can be taken away. Its question is 'what is THIS, and what happened to it?' — one record, in depth, which is what separates it from the list template. The four-part order is PROPOSED, not ruled.

identity.description: PROPOSED. An eyebrow (the record TYPE), a Status-indicator chip, an <h1> and a subtitle carrying the consequence in plain words. Putting the status IN the header rather than in the facts list is a choice and is Dave's.

actions.description: PROPOSED. Drawn quaternary / tertiary / primary, left to right, with the primary last — Button's own action-bar idiom. Whether a destructive action ('Cancel payment') belongs in a page header at all is Dave's.

tabs.description: PROPOSED. Drawn with the first tab selected. ⛔ SWITCHING IS `Tabs`' BEHAVIOUR AND IS NOT HOSTED HERE — the other three panels are not drawn, and the page says so on its own face. Whether a detail page should use tabs or one long column is Dave's.

facts.description: PROPOSED. A `Summary` key/value list ending in an emphasised total row. WHICH facts, and in what order, is a product decision.

history.description: PROPOSED. A `Timeline` inside a Stat-card surface rather than wearing its own card chrome — nesting a bordered card in a bordered card draws a box in a box. Timeline's own `.tl` background/border/padding are deliberately NOT copied; its container-type IS, because the reflow rule needs it.

documents.description: PROPOSED. `Document-row`s in the rail. ⚠ MEASURED AND REPORTED: in the primitive's 280px rail, document titles ellipsize at full desktop width ('Invoice INV-2026-0871' → 134px). That is Document-row's designed truncation meeting a narrow container. Whether a rail hosting document rows should be wide

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TemplateEmpty.description: What a whole PAGE says when it has nothing to show. Empty-state draws the empty REGION; this template supplies the three things only a page can know: the HEIGHT the region must hold, the page FURNITURE that stays visible around it (on a no-results page the search box and the filter chips are the entire recovery route), and the COUNT LINE that says what the page is empty OF.

variant.description: FIRST-RUN keeps the page's own primary action and repeats it inside the empty block. NO-RESULTS keeps the toolbar and offers a LINK back - never a second commitment.

minHeight.description: svh so a mobile browser's collapsing chrome cannot make the region taller than the screen.

apolloVariant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TemplateError.description: The page a person lands on when the address is wrong (404) or something failed at our end (500). It composes Confirmation's centred column and Empty-state's decorative glyph at page scale, and its whole design argument is what it does NOT do: it binds no RAG colour and it invents no support semantics. When: cause in (404, 500) AND RAG colour = unbound AND no support semantics invented AND one page serves ALL unexpected failures

variant.description: 404's primary action is the way back to something that exists. 500's primary action is to try the same thing again, because that is the only move the person can make.

referenceCode.description: Shown as neutral text. NOTHING is claimed about what it is for.

apolloVariant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TemplateListIndex.description: A PAGE-SCALE ORGANISM for a browse-and-find screen: a page header lock-up, ONE filter/toolbar bar, and a body of records with a pager. ⛔ IT DRAWS BOTH BODIES — a Data-grid table AND a Document-row list — with the same filters, the same five records and the same pager, because the library holds both answers and they are NOT interchangeable: a table carries relations BETWEEN rows (sort order, selection across a page, a column you can read down), a list carries one record per row and a tap target. Drawing both is a REFUSAL to settle a question that is Dave's, not a claim that a product ships both.

body.description: ⛔ THE STRUCTURAL QUESTION AND THE POINT OF THE PAGE. PROPOSED, NOT RULED. Whichever Dave picks, the other half of the reference file is deleted.

facets.description: PROPOSED. Drawn as native <select>s wearing Data-grid's own `.dg-pp select` chrome. ⛔ NOT a re-drawn Dropdown: Dropdown, Multi-select, Combobox and Date-range-picker all exist and all carry their own popup behaviour, and hosting one here would fork it. WHICH facet control a filter bar should use is

appliedFilters.description: PROPOSED. Dismissible chips (Data-grid's `.fchip`) plus a 'Clear all'. The chips are the only place the applied state is visible, which is why the empty result is drawn too.

selection.description: PROPOSED. Drawn with two rows selected and a bulk-action bar, because a selection bar that is never drawn is a state nobody reviews. Selection is tint + inset start bar + checked box — never colour alone.

pager.description: ⛔ A FINDING, NOT A CHOICE. This template consumes the GATED `Pagination` component. `Data-grid` ALSO carries its own pager, re-stating the recipe internally as `.pbtn`. Whether a grid should consume Pagination rather than duplicate it is Dave's.

emptyResult.description: PROPOSED wording, ruled shape. Data-grid's own `.dg-empty`: a reason, a suggestion and a real recovery action. Drawn because a list/index template that only shows its happy path hides the one state its own filter bar can create.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TemplateReport.description: A report page: a provenance-bearing report header, a stats band, charts, and the table that makes the charts auditable. A dashboard answers 'how are things right now'; a report is a CLAIM ABOUT A PERIOD, made at a MOMENT, from a stated SOURCE, and it has to be checkable. That difference is the template's whole contribution and it shows up in three places a dashboard has no need for: the provenance row, the table carrying the same figures the charts draw, and the footnote block.

period.description: The segmented switcher is drawn with three periods. The PERIOD COVERED, the PREPARED timestamp, the SOURCE and the CURRENCY are all mandatory in the provenance row - a report that cannot say where its numbers came from is decoration.

statTiles.description: Five, so the auto-fill grid has a reflow worth measuring rather than one worth asserting: MEASURED 4 -> 3 -> 1 tracks at 1400 / 820 / 420.

charts.description: ONE PER ROW, and that is arithmetic not taste - see antiPatterns.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TemplateSettings.description: The page where a person changes how their account behaves for them. It is an organism-of-organisms: a page-header lock-up, a column of SECTIONED form groups each on its own card surface, a rail carrying in-page navigation and the save state, and an action bar that stays reachable. It contributes page-scale LAYOUT, section RHYTHM and the setting-row relationship - every control inside it is a gated component, borrowed.

sections.description: Four are drawn: text fields, switches, a radio group plus a segmented control, and checkboxes plus a segmented control. Each is a <fieldset> on a Stat-card surface.

rail.description: The in-page jump list and the save-state panel. Present it is a 280px rail; absent the form column takes the full width. The rail moves BELOW the form when the split's CONTAINER is <=760px.

stickyActions.description: The action bar is position:sticky against the nearest SCROLLPORT. On a real page that is the page. See the antiPattern.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TemplateWizard.description: The page that walks a person through one task in ordered steps and ends with a receipt: progress indicator, one step visible at a time, a gated Next, a review step, and a confirmation. It contributes PAGE SCALE, real form steps, a review step and an end state - the step MECHANISM itself is Stepper's and is borrowed whole. When: steps >= 2 AND order is enforced AND next is gated AND a review step precedes the end AND the end is a receipt

steps.description: Drives the dots, the collapsed 'Step N of M' head, the track fill, the panels and the announcer from ONE source. The specimen carries four.

current.description: 1-based. Advancing is gated by the current step's rules; going BACK never is.

reviewStep.description: Renders Summary's dl with a Change control per row. Each Change carries the step index that owns the value.

endState.description: When 'confirmation', the wizard's own action bar RETIRES on the last step and Confirmation's own actions take over - two competing action bars would otherwise stack.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

Textarea.description: Multi-line text entry — the Input-fields boxed state channel stretched vertically. Vertical-only resize, live counter that warns by weight (never colour-alone) at 90% of the limit with polite announcements. Itinerary row 20 (P1); built Phase-2 wave 1. When: entry = free text AND the answer may run to more than one line AND there is no fixed option list AND a length limit is shown only where a real limit exists

maxlength.description: Drives the counter; remaining count announced politely at 90% and at the limit.

rows.description: Initial height; min-height 96px (4px grid), user resize vertical-only.

TimePicker.description: Payments scheduling: an Input-fields boxed field (free 24-hour HH:MM typing, validates on blur) plus a listbox of 30-minute slots opened from the time tail button — Dropdown's list language, scrolled to the chosen or nearest slot. Itinerary row 16 (P1); built Phase-2 wave 2 (worker A continuation).

value.description: HH:MM 24-hour. Free typing accepts any valid minute (14:37); the list offers the 48 half-hour slots.

step.description: Slot interval in minutes (30 = the reference; 15 doubles the list).

help.description: '24-hour format, like 14:30.' — the format hint doubles as the 3.3.3 suggestion.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

Timeline.description: The passive, ordered record of things that have already happened, where the time axis IS the structure: a vertical rail threading date-grouped entries, newest first. Two forms from one grammar — transaction history (status node + amount, the fintech case the itinerary names) and activity feed (actor avatar + what they did). When: records >= 2 AND time IS the structure AND every record has ALREADY HAPPENED AND entries are not buttons AND order is newest-first with date headings

form.description: history = status node + amount (transaction history); activity = actor avatar + what they did (activity feed). One grammar, two node treatments.

status.description: Colours the rail node AND the entry's status chip. The chip always carries a WORD, so the dot never carries meaning alone (s151-D1 clause 4).

grouped.description: Date group headings ('Today, 19 August'). Ungrouped is legal for short feeds but loses the axis the component exists for.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

Toast.description: A transient, elevated status message that confirms an event and leaves without being answered: appears bottom-of-viewport, auto-dismisses after ~6s (paused on hover/focus), never blocks the task. The snackbar of the feedback family — Alert is its persistent in-flow sibling, Banner its page-level one. Deliberately has NO error variant: errors demand persistent attention and route to Alert.

status.description: No error (snackbar precedent). Plain = statusless message ('Copied to clipboard.'), no glyph.

action.description: Optional single text action (e.g. Undo). The same action MUST exist somewhere persistent — a toast is missable by design.

duration.description: Auto-dismiss ms; timer pauses on hover/focus-within (2.2.1 pattern). Dismiss × always present.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

Tooltip.description: Provides contextual help relating to an element or area of a page — a small floating panel with a directional tip (pointer) revealed on hover/focus of a trigger (often a help icon).

tip.description: Which edge the pointer sits on (tooltip above vs below the trigger).

tipAlignment.description: Horizontal position of the pointer along that edge.

TransactionRow.description: A STATEMENT LINE IN A LEDGER: an ordered sequence of settled and pending entries with a RUNNING BALANCE, column headers, day grouping and a closing total. Its question is 'what was the balance after this?', which is a relationship between rows and therefore a table. PROPOSED #209 (itinerary row 91, slug transaction-row, P2) — NOT GATED, NOT RULED. Fintech semantics are Dave's (the Kpi-tile precedent, s182-D2).

entries.description: Ordered, newest first. Each entry: payee, reference line, one money value, and the balance AFTER it. Order is meaning here — a running balance cannot be reordered client-side without becoming false.

moneyColumns.description: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P1). 'two' = separate Money out / Money in columns, the UK statement convention, which carries the sign STRUCTURALLY. 'signed' = one Amount column carrying a U+2212. Both forms are DRAWN in the reference so Dave chooses by eye rather than from prose. Whichever he picks, the figu

runningBalance.description: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P3). This is the DISCRIMINATOR: with it false, the component IS a List-items transaction list and should be one. A pending entry shows an em dash, not a number, because the balance does not exist until it settles.

groupBy.description: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P5). Rendered as <th scope="rowgroup"> day headings. The alternative is a date column on every row — denser, equally buildable.

status.description: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P4). Rendered as a Status-indicator RAG-tint chip ALWAYS CARRYING ITS WORD; 'settled' draws no chip at all, because 400 green chips on a statement is noise. Which status maps to which chip tint is a SEMANTIC binding and is DAVE'S.

referenceLine.description: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P6). 'Card ending 4821 · Faster Payment'. Whether the method, the reference, the merchant category or none of them belongs on line 2 is unruled. It is the first thing to drop below 400c.

closingBalance.description: Rendered in a real <tfoot> so assistive technology announces it as a total rather than as another row.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

TransferList.description: Moves items between two labelled lists — 'Available' and 'Selected' — via checkboxes and move controls. Itinerary row 27 (P3, 'Move-between lists'), explicitly mapped to NOT be row 40's List-items ('⚠ NOT row 40's List-items (fuzzy matches on "list")'). Use where a user must build a subset FROM a larger set (assign accounts to a payee group, pick recipients for a standing instruction) and seeing both the chosen and unchosen sets at once matters more than a compact multi-select dropdown.

availableItems.description: Items shown in the left/'Available' panel. Each item is a checkable row (id + label).

selectedItems.description: Items shown in the right/'Selected' panel — the outcome of the control.

checkedIds.description: The currently ticked rows in EITHER panel — drives which items 'Move selected' acts on and which header checkbox shows checked/indeterminate/unchecked.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

Tree.description: A recursive disclosure list: nested nodes that open and close, one selectable at a time, depth carried by an indentation ladder and by aria-level. The shape for anything genuinely hierarchical — a corporate account structure, a category picker, a document tree — where a flat list would lose the containment relation. Built #210 wave 4 (heavy seven). PROPOSED, NOT RULED; every domain semantic is Dave's (the Kpi-tile precedent, s182-D2).

nodes.description: Recursive: each node is a label, an optional child list and an optional count. A node with a child list is a BRANCH and carries aria-expanded; a node without one is a LEAF.

selected.description: Single selection. Multi-select with checkboxes is NOT drawn — it would compose Selection-controls and it changes the aria contract (aria-multiselectable). Receipt Q11.

expanded.description: Which branches are open. Nothing is auto-expanded by the component.

lazy.description: A branch whose children are fetched on first open. While fetching, the node carries aria-busy and its group shows skeleton bones.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

VideoPlayer.description: Displays and controls digital video within a layout — play/pause, scrub, time and related controls overlaid on the video. Standard inline player and a larger hero variant.

variant.description: Standard inline player vs full-width hero player.

state.description: Playback states (multiple state rows shown on the page).

apolloVariant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

ViewOptions.description: A view control that lets users select different presentation formats of the same content (e.g. list vs grid). A segmented toggle of label-buttons or icon-buttons; the active format is the selected segment. When: NEVER

state.description: Per-segment; the chosen format is 'selected'.

variant.description: Apollo variants (meta.variants); first listed is the default by this probe's convention, not a ruling.

variants.name: standard
variants.use: Default accordion on white surfaces; titled section disclosure. Title uses the font-4 scale (covers display scales 1-3) or font-5.

variants.name: inline
variants.use: Compact, link-style disclosure for dense layouts or within running content; smaller footprint (size 5/6).

accessibility.role: Header is a button that controls a collapsible region (disclosure pattern)

variants.name: default
variants.use: Label + balance + meta row (type tag + status chip).

variants.name: minimal
variants.use: Label + balance only (no meta row).

accessibility.role: role="group" with aria-labelledby pointing at the account label, so the card is announced as a single unit.

variants.name: selector
variants.use: Choosing among the user's accounts in payment/transfer forms.

variants.name: chip
variants.use: Restating the chosen account in confirmations and summaries — compact, read-only.

accounts.use: The selectable accounts, each supplying name, masked number and balance.

accessibility.role: Trigger role="combobox" + aria-haspopup="listbox" + aria-expanded + aria-controls + aria-labelledby (label + value); menu role="listbox"; rows role="option" + aria-selected. Chip: role="group" + aria-label.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Tertiary Back on the left + secondary/primary pair on the right (wide container).

variants.name: sticky
variants.use: Same bar pinned to the bottom of a scrolling region.

actions.use: Holds the screen's primary and secondary actions; the container lays them out but never authors them.

accessibility.role: None on the bar itself (it is layout); the actions are native <button>s so they are focusable and keyboard-operable by default.

when.gate: the message is IN FLOW (inside the page or form it refers to) AND it persists until resolved or dismissed AND it carries a status glyph and a title, never colour alone AND an error alert never auto-dismisses
when.prose: CANON-ADJACENT — our own purpose already states the three-way rule: "Use Toast for transient confirmations and Banner for page-level persistent messages; use inline field validation (Input-fields) for single-control errors"; beats toast (proposed "transient, no answer required") whenever the reader must act; beats banner (proposed "the condition governs the whole page or session") whenever the message belongs to one form or section — Atlassian draws the identical line: "For messages with information affecting the whole site, use a banner"; yields to inline field validation for a single control.

variants.name: error
variants.use: Something failed and needs the user's attention now; assertive announcement.

variants.name: warning
variants.use: Caution or approaching deadline; amber surface always carries a near-black mark (R-D3).

variants.name: success
variants.use: In-flow confirmation that persists (contrast with Toast's transient success).

variants.name: information
variants.use: Neutral guidance or service notice.

accessibility.role: role="alert" for error (assertive); role="status" for warning/success/information (polite).

variants.name: display
variants.use: Hero balance / headline figure at 32px, bound to .t-cm-figure-4.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Inline body amount at 16px (in prose, list rows, summaries).

variants.name: small
variants.use: Dense numeric contexts at 14px (tables, ledger rows).

variants.name: redacted
variants.use: Value hidden for privacy; meaning carried by aria-label.

accessibility.role: Passive text by default. The redacted variant uses role="img" + aria-label so the masked value announces its meaning ('Balance hidden') rather than reading the dots.

variants.name: standard
variants.use: In-form amount field (GBP prefix + tabular figures).

variants.name: display
variants.use: Prominent single-question entry (You send £—) in payment journeys.

variants.name: bar
variants.use: sticky horizontal strip at the top of the scrolling region; the current section carries a bottom bar

variants.name: rail
variants.use: vertical list beside the content; the current section carries a leading bar and a surface change

variants.name: full
variants.use: a marketing site: a statement, four groups, and the legal bar a regulator requires

variants.name: short
variants.use: a servicing site whose end matter is a courtesy rather than a second navigation

brand.use: the masthead identity — the official masterbrand asset, bound #230 (masterbrand-light-colour on light chrome, masterbrand-dark-colour on dark).

primaryNav.use: AT MOST FOUR top-level destinations. The cap is the shell's argument, not a limitation.

content.use: the page. Rendered here as neutral placeholder furniture.

doormat.use: Footer in its FULL form. This is the shell's secondary navigation and it must not duplicate the masthead.

when.gate: primaryNavigation = absent AND breadcrumbs = absent AND search = absent AND exits = 1 AND job.count = 1
when.prose: the only frame defined by removal; beats every other shell (roles.json: all six carry navigation) whenever abandoning the task is the failure mode — authentication, a wizard, a passcode; yields to app-shell-top-nav the moment the user must be able to go somewhere else.

variants.name: auth
variants.use: sign in, register, one-time passcode, password reset

variants.name: task
variants.use: a payment, an application, an onboarding flow — anything with steps

brand.use: the masthead identity — the official masterbrand asset, bound #230 (masterbrand-light-colour on light chrome, masterbrand-dark-colour on dark).

exit.use: the ONE way out. A labelled control whose accessible name says what leaving does.

progress.use: form=task only. The screen's SINGLE accessible progress statement — see $finding-progress-collision.

task.use: the job. Rendered here as neutral placeholder furniture, deliberately not as content.

endMatter.use: Footer in its slim form. A doormat here would be a list of ways to abandon the task.

variants.name: three-pane
variants.use: a wide desktop window — rail, list and detail all visible

variants.name: two-pane
variants.use: a narrower window — the rail folds to the app bar's menu button, list and detail stay

variants.name: single-pane
variants.use: phone width — one pane at a time, with a back control in the detail header

listHeader.use: what the list is and how many rows it has. ⚠ NO FILTER OR TOOLBAR — see $finding-no-toolbar.

listRows.use: the master list. ⚠ THE LIBRARY HAS NO SUCH ATOM — see $finding-no-selected-list-row.

detailHeader.use: the record's name, a back control at narrow widths, and record-level actions

detail.use: the record. One region here is the real Skeleton-loader; the rest is placeholder furniture.

endMatter.use: Footer in its slim form, as the LAST CHILD OF `.sh` so it spans all three panes — the rail, the list and the detail are peers and none of them is 'the content column'. The doormat form fits the same slot.

variants.name: label
variants.use: a flat rail of five or six destinations, where the only missing information is the name

variants.name: menu
variants.use: a rail whose items have children — the flyout is where the second level lives, and the rail never grows to hold it

brand.use: a single-glyph identity in the 56px rail head. ⚠ A TEXT STAND-IN and, at 64px, the hardest place in the library to put a real masterbrand.

rail.use: the navigation, permanently. Icons at 18px in 64x44 targets, names carried in clip-path labels.

flyout.use: the name, or the children. Panel skin is Popover's; the contract depends on which — see $finding-two-contracts.

header.use: the 56px in-app band the content column opens with

content.use: the page. Rendered here as neutral placeholder furniture.

variants.name: expanded
variants.use: a wide desktop window — 248px of labelled destinations

variants.name: rail
variants.use: a narrower window, or a user who wants the room — 64px, glyphs only, every accessible name preserved

variants.name: off-canvas
variants.use: phone width — the column leaves the layout and becomes the drawer, carrying the same destinations

brand.use: the masthead identity — the official masterbrand asset, bound #230 (masterbrand-light-colour on light chrome, masterbrand-dark-colour on dark).

utilityActions.use: search, profile — 44x44 icon buttons in the app bar's trailing group

trail.use: the ancestor path above the page title

content.use: the page. Rendered here as neutral placeholder furniture — see App-shell-top-nav's $finding-skeleton-divergence, which states the reasoning once for all three shells.

endMatter.use: Footer in its slim form, placed INSIDE the content column (a child of .sh-content, not of .sh-body) so it stops at the nav column's edge — App-shell-nav-rail's own placement. The doormat form fits the same slot.

variants.name: horizontal
variants.use: two peer workspaces read side by side — a list of rows and the report about them

variants.name: vertical
variants.use: a live surface above its trail — a run monitor over its event log, where the lower pane grows and the upper one does not

chrome.use: masthead + trail, inherited whole from App-shell-top-nav

paneA.use: one of two COEQUAL panes. Rendered here as neutral placeholder furniture.

paneB.use: the other coequal pane. Same class, same chrome, same fence — that is what coequal means here.

when.gate: destinations <= 7 AND nav.levels <= 2
when.prose: the default for dashboards — the bento template composes it; beats app-shell-side-nav (roles.json when: "> 7 destinations or two nav levels") below those bounds and app-shell-nav-rail (when: "dense app, content cannot spare 248px") when the content can spare the column; yields to app-shell-multi-column (when: "list-and-detail job") and to app-shell-focused (when: "one job, no navigation (auth, wizard)") when the job has no navigation. Co-providers of page-frame are mutually exclusive by construction (roles.json §05: one-at-a-time facility), so no not-with is authored.

variants.name: inline
variants.use: a product with five or fewer primary destinations and a brand short enough to share the row

variants.name: stacked
variants.use: a product whose primary nav does not fit beside the brand, or one that needs a section tier under it

brand.use: the masthead identity — the official masterbrand asset, bound #230 (masterbrand-light-colour on light chrome, masterbrand-dark-colour on dark).

primaryNav.use: the top-level destinations, one marked aria-current="page"

utilityActions.use: search, profile, notifications — 44x44 icon buttons in the masthead's trailing group

trail.use: the ancestor path above the page title

content.use: the page. Rendered here as neutral placeholder furniture, deliberately not as content — see $finding-skeleton-divergence.

endMatter.use: Footer in its slim form; the doormat form fits the same slot

variants.name: image
variants.use: Avatar showing an uploaded photo; image opacity 100% default / 20% disabled (image/opacity tokens).

variants.name: initials
variants.use: Avatar showing the user's initials in medium-weight text on a subtle surface.

variants.name: icon
variants.use: Placeholder avatar showing a generic person icon when no image/initials available.

variants.name: group-announced
variants.use: the default — one accessible name for the set, discs hidden from AT; the set is the meaning

variants.name: roster
variants.use: a real list where every member is announced; use when the individuals ARE the content

variants.name: members-interactive
variants.use: each disc is its own 44px target linking to that person (medium and large only)

variants.name: group-target
variants.use: the whole stack is one 44px button — the correct answer for small stacks

variants.name: secondary
variants.use: The only tier specimen'd — a solid-but-not-primary control, consistent with 'never the primary action of the view'. Whether a tertiary/quaternary (lower-visibility) back-to-top should also exist is named in decisionsForDave.

accessibility.role: button

variants.name: simple
variants.use: A dot indicating new activity without a count (standalone 12px; on-icon 10/13/20px).

variants.name: number
variants.use: A badge showing a count of items (standalone 20px). Number text uses text/reverse on the primary fill, weight medium.

variants.name: on-icon
variants.use: Badge positioned on an icon; sizes small/medium/large to match icon size. NOTE: currently binds a deprecated surround token — see tokens / tokenValidation.

accessibility.role: REVIEW: badge is a decorative/status adornment on a host element; the host element (link/button/icon) is the focusable control

variants.name: error
variants.use: Page/session-level failure needing action; the ONE white-type surface IN BASE/MONO (type26-013 — white is red-only; fill #B92F1E, 6.02:1); assertive. s131-D1 (#131): in LEGACY white type also rides success and information — the red-only clause is base-scoped.

variants.name: warning
variants.use: Page-level caution; amber always carries near-black ink (R-D3).

variants.name: success
variants.use: Page-level confirmation that should persist; black ink (text/on-success, B-D6 precedent). s131-D1 (#131): legacy overrides text/on-success to WHITE on its teal #00847F (4.56:1).

variants.name: information
variants.use: Service notice; rag/text/on-information ink (minted s131-D1 #131 — base = the on-light dark ink; legacy reverses to white on its dark blue #305A85, 7.17:1). Formerly bound rag/text/on-light.

actions.use: Holds the banner's response actions; the container lays them out but never authors them.

accessibility.role: role="alert" for error (assertive); role="status" otherwise (4.1.3).

when.gate: shape = ancestor-path × links AND depth >= 2
when.prose: beats anchor-nav (roles.json when: "in-page, long document") when the trail is ancestry rather than in-page position; yields to navigations (when: "global — masthead / main-nav family") for global movement and to tabs (when: "local — peer views in one context") for peer views — it answers where-am-i, they answer where-can-i-go, so it complements rather than replaces them.

variants.name: default
variants.use: A clickable ancestor level (Small Print Link, font-6 regular).

variants.name: hover-pressed
variants.use: Interactive feedback for a level on hover/press. Shares text colour with default — differentiated by link styling (e.g. underline), not colour.

variants.name: no-link
variants.use: The current page — the final crumb, rendered as plain Small Print (non-link).

when.gate: emphasis in (primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary) AND label = text
when.prose: the default of the role; yields to icon-button (roles.json when: "space is tight and the glyph is universal") when label = glyph, to split-button (when: "one main action plus a menu of related ones") when a menu hangs off the action, and to links (when: "the action is navigation inside running text") when the action is navigation in prose.

variants.name: primary
variants.use: Highest-emphasis main action. Solid brand-red fill.

variants.name: secondary
variants.use: Alternative action. Solid black/near-black fill.

variants.name: tertiary
variants.use: Lower-emphasis action. Outlined (border) on a white fill.

variants.name: quaternary
variants.use: Lowest-emphasis / borderless (ghost) action; shares tertiary background tints on hover/press.

accessibility.role: button (or link styled as button when it navigates)

variants.name: standalone
variants.use: The month living in page flow — a journey step, a booking screen, a statement-period chooser. This is the component.

variants.name: narrow
variants.use: The same markup in a ~288px seat: columns are 1fr and cells keep their 40px minimum height, so it narrows with no breakpoint of its own.

variants.name: plain
variants.use: A static card header with no interactive affordance — read-only summary cards.

variants.name: inline-actions
variants.use: Two lightweight actions always visible (e.g. Edit / Pause on a standing order).

variants.name: status-overflow
variants.use: A verification/status chip plus a menu of less-frequent actions behind one overflow trigger — keeps the header from crowding as the action list grows.

variants.name: actions
variants.use: Card presenting an item with an action affordance (chevron). Content combos: icon/title/description in various pairings. Static surface (background/default).

variants.name: basic
variants.use: Interactive card (default/hover/pressed). Background shifts via tertiary/background tints on interaction. Built as a whole-card link (single tab stop).

variants.name: basic-non-interactive
variants.use: Static version of basic — no hover/pressed; background/default.

variants.name: image-with-border
variants.use: Card with an image plus headline (font-3) and optional headline link; bordered. Responsive image scales (3/5/6/7/8/9).

variants.name: image-without-border
variants.use: Image card without a border; responsive image scales.

content.use: The grouped content the card surface frames.

variants.name: standard
variants.use: One slide fills the viewport; prev/next arrows swap the visible slide, dots show position.

variants.name: peek/snap
variants.use: Native scroll-snap with neighbour slides peeking at both edges — signals 'there is more' without a caption saying so.

accessibility.role: The region carries aria-roledescription="carousel"; each slide carries aria-roledescription="slide" + aria-label="N of M" (APG naming pattern — first use in this repo, probe run at build: 0 pre-existing hits). Slide changes are NOT modelled as role=tab/tabpanel — a carousel slide is not an independent view the way a tab panel is (APG 2024 guidance).

variants.name: columns
variants.use: Every level visible at once. The hierarchy's shape is legible before anything is chosen; the panel is as wide as the levels need.

variants.name: stacked
variants.use: One level at a time with a back row, for a container too narrow for side-by-side columns. Reached by the .stacked class or automatically at a 420px container width.

accessibility.role: The trigger is a plain button carrying aria-expanded + aria-controls, deliberately NOT role=combobox — a combobox promises one popup of one type, and this popup is several listboxes. Each column is role=listbox with its own accessible name (which follows the branch it is showing), and its children are role=option carrying aria-selected. A branch that cannot be entered is aria-disabled, never removed.

when.gate: answers = comparison AND axis.x = categorical
when.prose: beats chart-line (roles.json when: "change-over-time") when the x-dimension is categorical rather than a time continuum, and beats chart-pie (when: "composition, no centre figure, ≤ 5 parts") when the parts do not sum to a whole; the stacked variant takes composition across categories, where it yields to chart-stacked-area (when: "composition over time") if the axis is time.

variants.name: column categorical (sortable)
variants.use: Compare categories; single series, ONE colour (dv-014); original/ascending/descending sort views.

variants.name: bar categorical
variants.use: Long category names / many categories; DV-D09 default fill = data/series/3 (orientation-distinct from the column's series/1).

variants.name: column status
variants.use: Counts by state (R-D9 ramp, direct-labelled — colour never alone, R-D6 A′).

variants.name: grouped column
variants.use: Multi-series comparison side-by-side (D-Q3); legend-as-filter + isolate + highlight; shaped+lettered swatches mirror on-chart keys.

variants.name: stacked column
variants.use: Part-to-whole per category (D-Q3); in-segment letter keys; legend-as-filter.

variants.name: no data
variants.use: Empty-state pattern in the chart frame.

series.use: One or more series drawn grouped or stacked across the categorical axis.

data.use: Carries the category values per series the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes.

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption; svg role="group"/"img" with a full-sentence data aria-label.

when.gate: answers = distribution AND categories >= 2 AND each category carries a five-number summary AND span.cols <= 8
when.prose: roles.json when: "distribution per category"; beats Chart-histogram (roles.json: "distribution, one variable") whenever the spread must be read PER CATEGORY; yields to it when variables = 1 and the bin shape is the claim.

variants.name: four categories
variants.use: Comparative distributions (e.g. team scores), whiskers to min/max, box = IQR, outliers marked separately.

categories.use: One entry per box on the categorical axis.

outliers.use: Points falling outside the whiskers, plotted individually.

data.use: Carries the five-number summary per category the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes.

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption; svg role="img" with a data-summary aria-label describing every category's median/IQR/whiskers/outliers.

when.gate: answers=comparison AND the reading is one measure against a target plus qualitative performance bands AND span.cols 4–6
when.prose: beats stat-card (60, "default — label · value · delta · period, no series") and kpi-tile (50, "a series exists to show") when the BENCHMARK, not the delta and not a series, is the point; yields to both when no target exists.

variants.name: three KPI rows
variants.use: Stacked horizontal gauges (e.g. revenue/satisfaction/retention) sharing one 0–100 domain.

rows.use: One measure/target row per KPI shown in the bullet stack.

ranges.use: The banded qualitative ranges each measure bar is read against.

data.use: Carries the measure, target and range values the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes.

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption; svg role="img" with a data-summary aria-label describing every row's measure and target.

when.gate: answers=comparison AND series=2 mirrored outward from a shared centre gutter AND categories ≥ 6
when.prose: beats chart-bar (grouped) when the two series must read as OPPOSED directions rather than adjacent columns; yields to Chart-butterfly-v (36, "as above, wide panel") when the category axis is ordered left-to-right and span.cols ≥ 8.

variants.name: mirrored horizontal, two series
variants.use: Compare two measures per category, both readable at a glance without stacking or grouping side-by-side.

series.use: The two opposed series mirrored either side of the centre gutter.

data.use: Carries the paired category values the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes.

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption; svg role="group" with a full-sentence data aria-label reading both series per category.

when.gate: answers=comparison AND series=2 mirrored above/below ONE horizontal baseline AND the category axis is ordered left-to-right (time, rank) AND span.cols ≥ 8
when.prose: yields to Chart-butterfly-h (40, "exactly two series mirrored, categories ≥ 6") whenever the categories are unordered or the panel is narrower than 8 cols; both yield to chart-bar for an ordinary grouped comparison.

variants.name: mirrored vertical, two series
variants.use: Compare two measures per category over a category axis that reads left-to-right (time, rank), both directions on the SAME scale so the halves stay comparable.

series.use: The two opposed series mirrored above and below the shared baseline.

data.use: Carries the paired category values the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes.

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption; svg role="group" with a full-sentence data aria-label reading both series per category.

when.gate: answers = change-over-time AND shape = periods × OHLC (open · high · low · close per session)
when.prose: roles.json when: "OHLC per period"; beats chart-line (roles.json: "change-over-time") only when all four price points per period are the claim; yields to chart-line whenever one measure's path is enough.

variants.name: forty sessions
variants.use: Realistic-density price series (ds-027 standing rule) — wick per session (ink @ reduced weight), body SOLID both directions, coloured by close-vs-open only.

data.use: Carries the OHLC values per period the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes.

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption; svg role="img" with a data-summary aria-label describing the series' range, open and close.

when.gate: answers=change-over-time AND series=2 AND units=different AND both read against ONE shared x (dv-line-006)
when.prose: beats chart-line (88, "change-over-time") on the different-units test and on nothing else; yields to chart-line (multi-series) or chart-bar (grouped) for a same-unit pair, which this meta's own antiPattern forbids drawing as a combo.

variants.name: combo
variants.use: Volume-style bars + a rate/average line in a different unit (e.g. payments processed + straight-through rate). NOT for two same-unit series — that is a multi-series line or grouped bar.

variants.name: no data
variants.use: Empty-state pattern in the chart frame.

series.use: The bar series on the primary axis plus the line series on the secondary axis.

data.use: Carries the both measures over the shared x the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes.

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption (names BOTH units and axes); svg role="group" + full-sentence aria-label; table panel role="region".

when.gate: answers=composition AND parts sum to a whole AND total=printed as a centre figure
when.prose: beats chart-pie (48, "composition, no centre figure, ≤ 5 parts") whenever the total is worth printing, and beats it on nothing else; yields to chart-stacked-area (64, "composition over time") when the split MOVES.

variants.name: spider + legend
variants.use: Default composition view; letters bridge chart ↔ legend (§04.3).

variants.name: direct labels
variants.use: Self-contained view (print/export-friendly); name + £value · % on each leader.

variants.name: no data
variants.use: Empty-state pattern in the chart frame.

slices.use: The parts of the whole drawn as ring segments.

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption; svg role="img", aria-label carries subject + total.

when.gate: answers = distribution AND variables = 1 AND bins = contiguous (no inter-bar gap) AND baseline = 0
when.prose: roles.json when: "distribution, one variable"; beats Chart-boxplot (roles.json: "distribution per category") when the frequency shape of ONE variable is the claim; yields to Chart-boxplot when categories >= 2; the no-gap rule is not cosmetic — the FT gives the same reason: "keep the gaps between columns small to highlight the 'shape' of the data".

variants.name: contiguous single-series
variants.use: Show the shape of a distribution across value bins. ONE colour (dv-014) — a histogram is not a categorical comparison, so bar's multi-hue categorical set does not apply.

bins.use: The contiguous frequency bins drawn as columns.

data.use: Carries the bin boundaries and counts the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes.

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption; svg role="group" with a full-sentence data aria-label reading every bin.

when.gate: answers=change-over-time AND series 1–5 on ONE continuous time axis AND axes=present AND span.cols ≥ 6
when.prose: the role's default at this intent, and it beats every sibling whose own `when` adds a further condition; yields to chart-combo (56, "two measures in different units over one axis") when units differ, to Chart-candlestick (44, "OHLC per period") when all four price points per period are the claim, and to chart-sparkline (30, "inline scale, no axes") when span.cols < 6.

variants.name: single series
variants.use: One measure over time; markers on every point, month labels along x.

variants.name: multi-series
variants.use: 2–5 measures; shapes + letters + legend names carry identity alongside colour.

variants.name: no data
variants.use: Empty-state pattern in the chart frame.

series.use: One polyline per series over the shared time axis.

data.use: Carries the values per point per series the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes.

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption; svg role="group" + aria-label (interactive children — role img would hide the marker focus stops); table panel role="region".

when.gate: answers=composition AND parts ≤ 5 AND total=not printed
when.prose: yields to chart-donut (80, "composition, a centre total is meaningful") whenever a centre total is wanted, which is the only thing separating the two; yields to chart-stacked-area (64) when the split moves over time.

variants.name: spider + legend
variants.use: Default composition view; letters bridge chart ↔ legend (§04.3).

variants.name: direct labels
variants.use: Self-contained view (print/export-friendly); name + £value · % on each leader.

variants.name: no data
variants.use: Empty-state pattern in the chart frame.

slices.use: The parts of the whole drawn as full-ring segments.

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption; svg role="group", aria-label carries subject + total.

when.gate: answers=relationship AND both axes carry quantitative measures
when.prose: the ONLY provider of relationship in the role, so it beats every sibling on the answers gate alone and needs no further test; yields to chart-combo (56) when the two measures share one x axis in different units instead of being plotted against each other. span.cols max 8 because a runtime fit is not baked (this meta's own responsive rule).

variants.name: single series
variants.use: One relationship (income × savings); circle markers, both-axis gridlines + numeric ticks.

variants.name: segments
variants.use: 2–3 groups; shapes + letters + legend names carry identity alongside colour (Everyday · Saver · Investor).

variants.name: no data
variants.use: Empty-state pattern in the chart frame.

series.use: Point sets, one per segment, sharing both quantitative axes.

data.use: Carries the x/y point values the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes.

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption; svg role="img" with a data-summary aria-label describing the relationship.

when.gate: answers=change-over-time AND series=1 AND axes=absent AND span.cols ≤ 4 (inline, or a trend cell in a table)
when.prose: yields to chart-line (88, "change-over-time") whenever the panel can carry axes, and is normally a complement of headline-metric rather than a chart-panel in its own right (ROLES-REVIEW §03).

variants.name: standalone
variants.use: A trend cell in tables/boards where the shape itself is the claim; table = the data surface.

variants.name: inline
variants.use: Inside a KPI tile next to an Amount-display value (the Stat-card seam — see $note).

variants.name: no data
variants.use: Compact dashed frame, title carries meaning.

data.use: Carries the trend values behind the axis-free line the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes.

accessibility.role: Standalone: figure role="group" + sr-only figcaption, svg role="group" with a trend-summary aria-label; the trend polyline = role="img" focus stop. Inline: aria-hidden — decorative; the composed value + period carry the meaning.

when.gate: answers spans change-over-time AND composition AND cumulative bands share ONE total across the time axis
when.prose: beats chart-donut (80, "composition, a centre total is meaningful") and chart-pie (48) when the split MOVES rather than being a snapshot; yields to chart-line (88, "change-over-time") when the total is not meaningful.

variants.name: 3-series stack
variants.use: Quarterly composition of a total (e.g. balances by product), one band per series, cumulative.

variants.name: no data
variants.use: Empty-state pattern in the chart frame.

series.use: The bands stacked cumulatively over the shared time axis.

data.use: Carries the values per point per band the chart renders, and the same rows the a11y data table exposes.

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption; svg role="group" + aria-label; table panel role="region".

variants.name: boxed
variants.use: Full-border field — the default, matching the boxed Input field.

variants.name: underline
variants.use: Bottom-stroke field — for forms already built on the underline style.

accessibility.role: input[role=combobox] + aria-autocomplete="list" + aria-expanded + aria-controls; the popup is role=listbox with role=option children carrying aria-selected. The highlight is aria-activedescendant, so focus never leaves the input.

variants.name: results
variants.use: the normal open state: a query, grouped results, one highlighted option

variants.name: empty
variants.use: the query matches nothing — a live-region message plus a recovery hint

variants.name: success
variants.use: Completed-successfully screen (rag/success glyph). Built here.

actions.use: Holds the next actions offered after the flow completes; the container lays them out but never authors them.

accessibility.role: role='group' with aria-labelledby pointing at the title, so the panel is announced as a unit.

variants.name: inline
variants.use: Circular graphic indicator beside the time value.

variants.name: stacked
variants.use: Compact stacked layout (indicator + value), narrow footprint.

variants.name: undecorated
variants.use: Time value only, no graphic indicator.

variants.name: centered
variants.use: A full-bleed marketing band — a page section whose whole job is the call to action.

variants.name: split
variants.use: A narrower in-page band — a call to action that sits between other content, e.g. at the end of an article or a feature grid.

variants.name: default
variants.use: group row on, comfortable density, a filter on every text column — the transactions board header

variants.name: compact
variants.use: data-density=compact: 32px header row, 32px targets, 4px cell padding; for a dense back-office console where the operator wants rows, not air

variants.name: no-group-row

No field count, row count or column count gates this (s274-D4): the comparison test decides — if a field must be read DOWN a column across records, it is a table, not a list. A list-level heading is OPTIONAL on all three containers (s274-D5); a per-card title is a ROW field, distinct from the list heading. Beats table (roles.json when: "default, read-mostly") and data-grid (when: "sort / filter / select / edit-in-place is required") whenever each record is read across its own row; yields to timeline (when: "time is the structure, records have happened") and to tree (when: "records nest").

when.gate: the content is STRUCTURED and FOCUSABLE AND it opens on CLICK from a labelled trigger AND it does not scroll AND it is non-modal (no focus trap, no aria-modal) AND only one is open
when.prose: CANON-ADJACENT — our purpose already carries the three-way rule: "If the user can act inside it, it is a Popover; if it is a sentence of help text, it is a Tooltip; if it must interrupt, it is a Modal"; Atlassian states both halves independently ("For interactive overlays, use the modal dialog component" / "For non-essential, non-interactive messages, use the tooltip component"); yields to drawer or modals once the content scrolls (our antiPatterns[2], Atlassian: "Don't make popups that scroll", Carbon: past four columns wide use a modal).

variants.name: explainer
variants.use: Why-we-ask / policy context beside a form field, with a follow-up link.

variants.name: detail
variants.use: Fee breakdowns, calculation detail — structured content too rich for a tooltip.

content.use: The structured, focusable content the popover holds.

accessibility.role: Non-modal dialog: role="dialog" + aria-labelledby, NO aria-modal. Trigger: aria-haspopup="dialog" + aria-expanded + aria-controls.

variants.name: fixed-plate
variants.use: The symbol keeps a white plate and dark modules in every theme, because it binds mode-invariant tokens (surface/digital-black on text/reverse — the same hex in light and dark). Dark-on-light is what ISO/IEC 18004 specifies and what every reader handles.

variants.name: follows-theme
variants.use: The symbol binds the page's own text and background, so it inverts in dark mode: light modules on a dark field. Visually calmer inside a dark surface; tolerated by many modern scanners and not by all of them.

accessibility.role: role="img" with an aria-label that says what the code is FOR, not what it looks like. The matrix itself is decorative to assistive technology — the payload is what matters and it is carried in text.

variants.name: icon
variants.use: Icon shortcut + font-7 label.

variants.name: avatar

variants.name: default
variants.use: Two handles, a filled band between them, min/max value pair shown as text.

accessibility.role: Two real <input type="range"> elements, each with its own aria-labelledby (sharing the field's one visible label) and a live aria-valuetext ('£200, minimum' / '£800, maximum') so AT never has to infer which handle is which from position alone.

variants.name: input
variants.use: A real fieldset of 5 native radio buttons the user can set — 'Rate this product'.

variants.name: readOnly
variants.use: A passive aggregate score, e.g. on a product or review card.

accessibility.role: Input variant: a real <fieldset>/<legend> containing role="radiogroup" (implicit, via 5 grouped native <input type="radio">) — the SAME native-keyboard idiom Selection-controls already earns honestly for grouped Radio ('native checkbox/radio/switch have NO JS keyboard model by design'), copied rather than hand-rolled. Read-only variant: role="img" with the full sentence ('Rated 4.3 out of 5') as its accessible name; the star row itself is aria-hidden.

variants.name: drag-handle
variants.use: Grab handle (icon/default); hover fills the target with tertiary/background/hover. Cursor changes grab→grabbed while dragging.

variants.name: drop-zone-highlight

variants.name: tight

variants.name: emphasis
variants.use: 8px rule where the coverage is the primary content of its region. Progress-bar's .pb-lg size.

accessibility.role: The readout is role="group" + aria-labelledby. The bar is role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/valuemin/valuemax and a full aria-valuetext, copied from Progress-bar's non-percentage specimen.
Use role=search / combobox semantics for predictive search; expose aria-expanded + aria-activedescendant for the suggestion list

variants.use: On/off toggle. On-track dark, off-track white; disabled track greys (deprecated).

variants.name: expanded
variants.use: the default desktop column: icon + label, group headings visible

variants.name: rail
variants.use: collapsed to 64px, icon-only, labels visually hidden but present in the accessibility tree

variants.name: overlay
variants.use: Under 768px the same column slides in over a scrim from a menu button. Escape or the scrim closes it and focus returns to the button. One class (.is-narrow on the frame), no forked markup.

variants.name: text block
variants.use: Heading + body lines while copy loads.

variants.name: list rows
variants.use: Avatar + two lines, mirrors List-items.

variants.use: Media + copy + control inside a bordered shell, mirrors Cards.

accessibility.role: The region carries role="status" + aria-busy="true" + a visually-hidden 'Loading content'; every bone is aria-hidden — ONE announcement per region, not per bone (4.1.3).

variants.name: double
variants.use: Two handles selecting a min/max range.

accessibility.role: Use role=slider (single) / two thumbs for range, each with aria-valuemin/max/now and an accessible name

variants.name: primary
variants.use: The main action IS the primary action of its context (e.g. 'Send payment' with 'Schedule for later' as an alternative).

variants.name: tertiary
variants.use: A lower-emphasis split action (e.g. 'Export' with format alternatives) that should not compete with a page's real primary button.

variants.name: horizontal
variants.use: Two panes side by side; the bar is vertical and Left/Right resize it.

variants.name: vertical
variants.use: Two panes stacked; the bar is horizontal and Up/Down resize it.

variants.name: fixed
variants.use: A boundary without a control. Still a separator, still named, no longer resizable.

accessibility.role: role=separator with tabindex=0, aria-orientation naming the orientation OF THE BAR, aria-controls pointing at the primary pane, and aria-valuemin / aria-valuemax / aria-valuenow / aria-valuetext publishing where the boundary is. The fixed variant keeps role=separator and its name but drops the tab stop and sets aria-disabled.

variants.name: standing-order
variants.use: Fixed amount, fixed rhythm, the customer's own instruction. Shows sort code and account ending.

variants.name: direct-debit
variants.use: The payee pulls. Shows the service-user reference, and 'Amount varies' where the next figure is unknown.

variants.name: paused
variants.use: Still yours, still returns. The row is NOT dimmed — a paused mandate is live information.

variants.name: failed
variants.use: The last payment did not go through. A WORD on the warning seat plus a plain consequence line. No red.

variants.name: ending-soon
variants.use: A mandate with an end condition: '2 payments left', 'until 20 August 2026'.

variants.name: cancelled
variants.use: History. FULLY LEGIBLE, with a 'Cancelled' chip; only the control is disabled. See the $renderFinding — the dimmed version was drawn and could not be read.

accessibility.role: A <ul> of PASSIVE <li> rows, each holding a stretched-link primary (<a> whose ::after covers the row) and a SIBLING <button>. Document-row's shape, copied: nesting an interactive control inside a <button> is invalid (4.1.1), unreachable in several ATs, and swallows the inner accessible name.

when.gate: shape = one-measure × value-and-delta AND series = none AND delta != none
when.prose: the default of the role; beats kpi-tile (roles.json when: "a series exists to show (s247-D3 / DP-08: no series ⇒ not a KPI tile)") exactly when no series exists, and beats Chart-bullet (when: "a target or performance band is the point, not the delta") when the delta, not a band, is the claim.

variants.name: display
variants.use: Primary board tiles — 32px value.

variants.name: compact
variants.use: Dense boards / sidebars — 24px value.

variants.name: flat
variants.use: No movement: 'No change', full ink, no arrow.

accessibility.role: role="group" + aria-label naming metric and period, so the tile reads as one unit.

variants.name: heading-only
variants.use: Section heading + a 3-tile Stat-card board — the default, matching Template-dashboard's own KPI section.

variants.use: Section heading + a 4-tile Kpi-tile board with sparklines — a dense band that shows trend shape, not just the number.

variants.name: heading-action
variants.use: Section heading + a trailing 'View all' link + a wider board — for a band that is a preview of a longer list elsewhere.

when.gate: shape = one-state × dot-and-label AND span.cols <= 4
when.prose: the default of the role; beats summary (roles.json when: "n × count as a key/value list, 6–12 cols") whenever exactly one state is read; yields to badge (when: "inline, attached to another element, count only") when the dot is attached to another element rather than standing alone.

variants.name: wide (dots)

steps.use: The per-step content panels the stepper drives.

when.gate: shape = rows × name-value-pairs AND rows >= 2 AND span.cols >= 6
when.prose: beats status-indicator (roles.json when: "one state, one dot + label, 2–4 cols") whenever more than one row must be read at once; yields to meter (when: "the threshold is a cap being spent against (limits-meter reading)") when threshold = cap-spent-against, and to badge (when: "inline, attached to another element, count only") when the reading is inline.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Plain name→value rows.

variants.name: with-total
variants.use: Adds an emphasised total row as the last row.

accessibility.role: Semantic <dl>/<dt>/<dd> so assistive tech announces each name→value pair as a group (1.3.1). Each row wraps one dt+dd in a div.

variants.name: standard
variants.use: Full-width bar with icon + label per destination; current item filled.

variants.name: segmented
variants.use: Segmented control spanning the full screen width, icon-only (Home / Cards / Payments / Insights), elevated; the selected fill is a PILL that slides between segments (same easing as the toggle / View-options), black + white glyph (inverts in dark). #261 N2, Dave verbatim: "the segmented island was better in the original, one change: I ruled that entire lock-up was mutually exclusive, I've changed my mind about the menu button". So Menu is a separate circular button OUTSIDE the island AND outside its exclusive group: a disclosure carrying aria-expanded that never clears the island's current destination, and the fill no longer collapses. It matches the lozenge height and keeps the inverting fill + 4px surface ring for its open state. The island geometry is 7647aaf's, verified by rendering both. EXPLORATION — rounding + elevation depart from the flat/angular brand.

items.use: The 3-5 equal-width destinations, each an icon plus label.

accessibility.role: <nav aria-label> wrapping the destinations; the current item carries aria-current='page'.

variants.name: tag
variants.use: Static keyword label; font-6 (small) / font-7 (extra-small); optional filled chip.

variants.name: tag-link
variants.use: Interactive tag (filter/navigate); font-6/7 regular-link; default + hover/pressed.

variants.name: with tags
variants.use: The working state — chips wrap inside the field and the counter reports how many remain.

variants.name: empty
variants.use: A plain one-row field, so it never looks broken before use; the help text states how a value is committed.

accessibility.role: A plain text input — deliberately NOT role=combobox, because there is no list to expand and claiming one would be a lie to AT. Each chip's dismiss is a real button with a purposeful accessible name ('Remove INV-4471').

variants.name: logon
variants.use: Username + password, with a reveal toggle, a create-account route and a help route.

variants.name: register
variants.use: Name + email + new password, with the password requirements stated BEFORE the field and kept visible.

variants.name: otp
variants.use: Secure-entry's gated code cells with the resend countdown, placed in the auth frame.

accessibility.role: No invented roles. The error box is role=alert with tabindex=-1; the OTP cells are a role=group named by their label; the OTP message is role=status.

when.gate: position = end of an instruction AND order = message, then FACTS, then actions, then what-happens-next AND a reference is shown if one exists
when.prose: beats the Confirmation component (roles.json feedback role) because a confirmation PAGE is also the RECEIPT — that reordering is the template's whole contribution; ends a flow that template-wizard began.

variants.name: success
variants.use: The instruction is complete and irreversible from here. Roundel, entrance animation, a receipt Summary with an emphasised total, two equal actions, three next steps.

variants.name: pending
variants.use: Accepted but NOT finished. No roundel, no green, no entrance pop: a decorative glyph at alpha/40 and a Status-indicator chip carrying the meaning in a word, plus the expiry stated plainly.

accessibility.role: No invented roles. Each specimen is a <main> whose message column is role="group" with aria-labelledby on the <h1>; each receipt is a real <dl> labelled by its panel heading; each next-steps list is an <ol>.

variants.name: create
variants.use: A new record. Empty fields, no destructive action, no dirty state.

variants.name: edit
variants.use: An existing record. Prefilled, dirty-state strip, destructive action, optionally locked fields.

accessibility.role: No invented roles. The app bar is a <header>, the page body a <main>, the guidance panel an <aside> with aria-labelledby, the form-level error box role="alert" with tabindex=-1 so focus can land on it.

variants.name: default
variants.use: The drawn page: 4 KPIs, one chart panel, a two-card rail, a 6-row grid.

variants.name: narrow
variants.use: Below ~760 CONTAINER px the split collapses to one column and the KPI board goes to a single track. Both are the primitives' own behaviour — once the split has a container HOST.

variants.name: default
variants.use: The drawn page at six columns: one full-width KPI group of four modules, then a chart group beside a position group.

variants.name: banded
variants.use: The wall's own container queries re-column it at 1100 / 820 / 520 CONTAINER px to 3 / 2 / 1. Every group becomes a single column and every module a full row. That is canon's compiled behaviour, not a variant this file declares.

variants.name: default
variants.use: The drawn page: identity + tabs + facts + history in the main column, documents + a payee summary in the rail.

variants.name: narrow
variants.use: Below ~760 CONTAINER px the split collapses and the rail follows the main column. The tab strip scrolls horizontally rather than wrapping.

variants.name: first-run
variants.use: Nothing exists yet. Empty-state's first-run form: decorative glyph, title, one line of body, ONE action - a primary Button.

variants.name: no-results
variants.use: Records exist; this filter matched none. The search box and three filter chips STAY on screen, a count line reads '0 of 1,284 transactions' in a role="status", and the single action is a link back.

accessibility.role: No invented roles. Each specimen is a <main> with an <h1>; the empty regions are <section aria-labelledby>; the filter chip bar is role="group" with an accessible name.

when.gate: cause in (404, 500) AND RAG colour = unbound AND no support semantics invented AND one page serves ALL unexpected failures
when.prose: beats template-empty (proposed "the query succeeded and returned nothing") because here the page could not be produced at all; beats an inline Alert (slice A) because the failure is the PAGE, not a field.

variants.use: The address is wrong. 'We cannot find that page' + 'Nothing on your account has been affected.'
Something failed at our end. 'This was not caused by anything you did, and no payment or instruction was submitted.'

accessibility.role: No invented roles. Each specimen is a <main> whose message column is role="group" with aria-labelledby pointing at the <h1>.

variants.use: Data-grid. Sortable columns, page-scoped selection, a bulk bar, a range read-out and a rows-per-page control.

variants.name: field error
variants.use: A setting fails a rule. Drawn on the Security section: Selection-controls' error ATOM (s151-D1 clause 3 - the atom takes the red, the label keeps default ink) plus an .err-msg carrying a symbol AND a sentence.

when.gate: steps >= 2 AND order is enforced AND next is gated AND a review step precedes the end AND the end is a receipt

when.gate: entry = free text AND the answer may run to more than one line AND there is no fixed option list AND a length limit is shown only where a real limit exists

variants.name: closed
variants.use: Resting field with the time tail glyph.

variants.name: open
variants.use: Anchored listbox (~5.5 rows, scrolls): 44px options, tabular figures so the column aligns, selected = weight 500 + neutral tick.

when.gate: records >= 2 AND time IS the structure AND every record has ALREADY HAPPENED AND entries are not buttons AND order is newest-first with date headings
when.prose: roles.json when: "time is the structure, records have happened"; beats list-items when the date rail is the reading rather than a sort order; yields to list-items inside a date group the moment entries must open (our AP1), and never borrows Progress-tracker's aria-current because there is no current step (our AP0).

variants.name: history
variants.use: transaction history — status node, amount, optional explanatory line

variants.name: activity
variants.use: activity feed — actor avatar replaces the status node; who did what, when

variants.name: empty
variants.use: no activity in the window; a single line of prose, no rail

variants.use: Transient confirmation of a completed event (payment sent, message archived).

variants.name: information
variants.use: Passive notice (draft saved, new version available).

variants.name: warning
variants.use: Non-blocking caution (connection unstable). If action is required, use Alert instead.

variants.name: plain
variants.use: Statusless micro-confirmation, no glyph.

variants.use: Two panels side by side with a four-button move column between them (single/all, both directions).

variants.use: The drawn component: one selected node, aria-selected, a mono leading bar.

variants.use: Text segments (e.g. 'List' / 'Grid').
